audit.why: 53.61% over 194 games matches the arc: even level 1, Cassiopeia's from 2 through the first item on grounded dashes, Yasuo's once crit comes online. Early/mid/side-lane framing holds.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the full layer calls Wind Wall's downtime a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s and lasts 4 seconds, so the window is closer to twenty seconds at rank 1 — and that window, not a level, is what times your commits.
audit.corrected: Put 25s at rank 1 into the spikes and the cooldown breakdown and corrected the downtime figure.

audit.whatIsWrong: The biggest error in this matchup. The content layer says three separate times that 'none of your damage is a projectile, so Windwall blanks nothing' and that 'Windwall does nothing in this lane'. Twin Fang IS a projectile and Wind Wall blocks it — that is your entire damage engine. The full layer overcorrects the other way and claims Wind Wall 'blocks Q and E both', which is also wrong: Noxious Blast is a placed ground zone.
audit.why: Riot text: Wind Wall — 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds.' The kit file flags Twin Fang as projectile and Noxious Blast as zone. Advice built on 'the wall does nothing' will get the reader killed walking into a wall with fangs on cooldown.
audit.corrected: Stated the split cleanly everywhere: Noxious Blast goes through the wall, Twin Fang does not, so poke with Q while it is up and cash the fang chain the moment it expires.

audit.why: Miasma grounding Sweeping Blade is correctly identified and is the second pillar of the matchup — Sweeping Blade is a dash on a sub-second cooldown, so grounding it is what makes him stand still in the poison.

edits.before: With Q+E you prime with Noxious Blast then chain Twin Fang for the increased poisoned-target damage. None of it is a projectile, so his Windwall is dead weight here and he just eats the DPS.
edits.after: With Q+E you prime with Noxious Blast then chain Twin Fang for the poisoned-target bonus. Wind Wall eats the fangs but not the placed Q zone, so poke through it and cash the chain once it drops.

edits.before: Poke with Noxious Blast freely — none of your damage is a projectile, so Windwall blanks nothing and he can't deny your engine
edits.after: Poke with Noxious Blast through Wind Wall — a placed zone ignores it — and hold Twin Fang, which is a projectile, until the wall expires

edits.before: At 2 your Q-into-Twin-Fang trade beats his Q poke for the bonus poisoned-target damage, and crucially his Windwall walls neither your placed Q zone nor your point-blank E.
edits.after: At 2 your Q-into-Twin-Fang trade beats his Steel Tempest poke on poisoned-target damage, but Wind Wall blocks the fangs — only the placed Noxious Blast zone goes through it.

edits.before: Level 1 is a coinflip — you have one ability and no poison to stack, his Q out-pokes your single Noxious Blast, so just farm safely. The moment you hit 2 with Q+E, start priming: land Noxious Blast on him, then Twin Fang does its bonus poisoned-target damage and refunds. His Windwall does nothing in this lane — your Q is a placed ground zone and your E is a point-blank nuke, neither is a projectile to wall. At 3, drop Miasma the instant he winds up an E; the ground cancels his dash and he's stuck eating poison.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coinflip — one ability, no poison to stack, and Steel Tempest out-pokes a single Noxious Blast, so farm safely. From 2 with Q+E, start priming: land Noxious Blast, then Twin Fang for the poisoned-target bonus and the refund. Know the wall — Noxious Blast is a placed ground zone and passes it, but Twin Fang is a projectile and Wind Wall eats it, so poke with Q while the wall is up and save the fangs for after it drops. At 3, drop Miasma as he winds up Sweeping Blade; grounded, the dash dies and he stands in the poison.

edits.before: This is your lane. Ranks in Q and E mean you out-DPS him in any extended trade, and your passive move speed (no boots) plus Q's speed-on-hit let you kite his dashes. The whole matchup is Miasma: every time he E's onto you or through a minion, the ground cancels it and you walk away chaining Twin Fangs. At 6, hold Petrifying Gaze for his all-in — stun him mid-commit and the trade becomes a kill. Just respect his Steel Tempest stacks: eating the third-hit knockup mid-combo lets him reset the trade and ult you.
edits.after: This is your lane. Ranks in Q and E mean you out-DPS him in any extended trade, and Serpentine Grace plus Q's speed-on-hit let you kite his dashes. The matchup is Miasma: every time he Sweeping Blades onto you or through a minion, the ground cancels it and you walk away chaining Twin Fang. Wind Wall is 25 seconds at rank 1 and lives four — while it stands, poison with Q and spend the fangs the second it expires. At 6, hold Petrifying Gaze for his all-in and respect Steel Tempest stacks: the third-hit knockup feeds his ult.

edits.before: Once Yasuo finishes IE he takes the matchup back — he's a hard scaler with passive double-crit, and you stay squishy with no resistances. His crit autos shred you and his R chains off any knockup. Windwall still doesn't matter for your damage (none of it is a projectile), but his raw crit DPS no longer needs it. Close the game on your item spike; if it goes long you can't 1v1 a fed Yasuo, so group, save Miasma to ground his teamfight engage, and use Petrifying Gaze to answer his all-in rather than dueling him in a side lane.
edits.after: Once Yasuo finishes IE he takes the matchup back — he is a hard scaler with passive double-crit, and you stay squishy with no resistances. His crit autos shred you and his R chains off any knockup. Wind Wall still eats your Twin Fang, so a well-timed wall now blanks a whole rotation instead of a trade. Close the game on your item spike; if it goes long you cannot 1v1 a fed Yasuo, so group, save Miasma to ground his teamfight engage, and use Petrifying Gaze — which is not a projectile — to answer his all-in rather than duelling him in a side lane.

edits.before: Wind Wall blocks Q and E both, but Miasma grounds his dashes — an honest fight between his wall cooldown and your zone.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks the fangs but not the Q zone, and Miasma grounds his dashes — a fight between his wall and your cloud.

edits.before: Ground the engage, stun the commit, and melt him in the E-spam. Nothing here works through Wind Wall — schedule your pattern around its cooldown.
edits.after: Ground the engage, stun the commit, and melt him in the E-spam. Twin Fang dies to Wind Wall, so schedule the chain around its 25 seconds.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. It governs your forward steps. - W Miasma spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — 25s at rank 1, four seconds of it standing. It blocks Twin Fang, not the placed Q zone, so poke through and hold the fangs. - W Miasma spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.after: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the twenty-second invitation.

Bad trade: Spamming E without poison until your mana bar dies — or firing the whole fang chain straight into a fresh Wind Wall.

notes: Highest-value fix in this slice: the content layer asserted four times that Wind Wall blanks nothing against Cassiopeia. Twin Fang is flagged projectile in the kit file and Wind Wall blocks all enemy projectiles, so the old advice inverted the matchup's central rule. Petrifying Gaze is not flagged as a projectile so I treated it as passing the wall, but that is Medium confidence and I kept the claim to a single clause.
